## Review and fix of solution for rm-07782

I verified the entire solution against an exhaustive model checker (all reflexive-transitive frames of size <=3, all hereditary bi-valuations) and by structural reasoning. **All substantive mathematical claims hold.** Confirmed:

- **Base 2C:** Aristotle's theses ~(A->~A), ~(~A->A) and both Boethius directions hold globally in the +-fragment; duals in the - -fragment.
- **Separation invariant:** truth set of any strong-negation-free formula is independent of V^- (spot-checked, 0 violations; induction is clean since no clause in the negation-free language mentions V^-).
- **Undefinability of ~ and of the constants:** the witness models in the proof check out exactly.
- **Collapse of connexive theses:** with the only available negation neg A := A->bot, both Aristotle neg(p->neg p) and Boethius (p->q)->neg(p->neg q) are +-unverified. Witness confirmed.
- **2C^{-~} negation-inconsistent yet non-trivial:** bot->p is globally proved AND globally refuted; p not provable. Confirmed.
- **2C^{-~,-c} negation-consistent:** no constant-free formula is ever globally refuted (0 counterexamples).

### Fix applied
The only genuine defect was the **proof of Theorem `thm:nocon`** (collapse of the connexive theses): the original argument wandered through several instances that do *not* refute Aristotle (vacuous-truth cases) before reaching a working witness, and the Boethius part was merely asserted. I rewrote the proof to use a **single clean countermodel**: the one reflexive world with V^+(p)=V^+(q)=empty. There:
- p->neg p holds vacuously, so neg(p->neg p) is +-unverified (it would need some v with v|=+bot) -> Aristotle fails;
- p->q and p->neg q both hold vacuously, so neg(p->neg q) is +-unverified, hence (p->q)->neg(p->neg q) has a verified antecedent and unverified consequent -> Boethius fails.

Both failures re-confirmed numerically. No other changes were needed; the calculi, twist-algebra completeness sketch, definability map, and master summary are sound as written. The fix is in solution.tex.
